standard_prerequisites.name: Localization of a topos at a sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the topos structure of the localization and the reduction to the representable case.

core_obligations: Import from the sites-level localization lemma that Sh(C)/F is a topos and the associated basic properties (proof lines 2765-2768).
Identify j_F^{-1}O with O_F and conclude that O_F is a sheaf of rings, so that the structure map j_F^sharp may be chosen to be the identity (proof lines 2769-2773).

Reduce to the case where C has all finite limits with subcanonical topology and F = h_U for an object U, and derive the description of j_{F!} from the explicit description in that case, completing the proof up to line 2782 (proof lines 2774-2782).
proof_roadmap: Get the topos structure of the localization from the sites lemma.
Identify the structure sheaf with the pullback and set the structure map to the identity.
Reduce to the representable case with finite limits.
difficulty_reason: The lemma endows the localization of a topos at a sheaf F with a structure sheaf O_F, making it a ringed topos, and produces the canonical morphism of ringed topoi to the original, together with the expected descriptions of the functors involved. The proof imports from the sites-level localization lemma that the localized category is a topos and the basic properties, identifies the pullback of the structure sheaf with O_F using that lemma, and hence may take the structure map j_F^sharp to be the identity; it further reduces to the case where the site has finite limits with a subcanonical topology and F is representable, where the remaining description follows from the explicit description of the lower shriek functor (proof lines 2764-2782). H2: the identification of the structure sheaf and the reduction to the representable case are the substance.
